To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

biased molecular dynamics simulations can be used to generate a collection of pocket-containing conformations for a protein, and that the shape of the pocket can be used to identify small molecules that complement it.

(1) we have developed a new, ultra-fast method for virtual screening of small molecules against protein-protein interaction targets; (2) this method is based on the concept of "pocket optimization," where the shape and chemical properties of the protein surface is optimized to bind a perfect, nonphysical, pseudomolecule; and (3) the shape of this pseudomolecule is used as a pharmacophore to search chemical libraries for potential inhibitors of the protein target.

1) biased molecular dynamics can be used to build an ensemble of protein conformers with optimized pockets for ligand binding, and 2) these pocket conformers, and the corresponding exemplars, can be used to identify small-molecule ligands that bind at protein-protein interaction sites.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel methods for computational ligand discovery, and in particular with the application of such methods to the challenging task of protein-protein interactions.
the design and development of novel computational approaches for structure-based virtual screening of large chemical libraries.

developing computational methods that enable rapid and accurate screening of chemical libraries for small molecules that modulate protein-protein interactions, and that are therefore of interest for drug discovery.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
exemplar screening is a powerful and fast alternative to traditional docking for identifying ligands that bind to protein interaction sites.
the exemplar-based virtual screening is a promising approach for identifying inhibitors of protein-protein interactions.
this approach is a very powerful tool for virtual screening and drug discovery.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
exemplar-based screening provides an effective, ultra-high-throughput approach for identifying small-molecule inhibitors of protein interaction sites.
this approach enables ultra-high-throughput screening for small-molecule inhibitors of protein-protein interactions.
this approach enables a "structure-based" virtual screening workflow for protein-protein interactions, without the requirement of a crystal structure of a bound protein-ligand complex.
The main takeaway from our work is that

exemplar-based virtual screening is a viable alternative to docking for screening large compound libraries, and that the combination of pocket optimization, exemplar screening, and ensemble docking provides an effective strategy for identifying diverse small-molecule inhibitors of protein-protein interactions.

, by leveraging the information contained within a single, high-resolution protein structure, we can identify a diverse collection of ligand-like compounds that bind to the protein surface, and thus potentially inhibit its function.
, for the first time, it is possible to perform high-throughput screening of chemical compounds at protein interaction sites with the same efficiency as traditional binding pockets.
